sets.title: Grow a Better Plant Draft
sets.titleEs: Mejora el borrador de la planta

learn.rule: To revise, swap vague words for exact words, add a signal word, and add missing details.
learn.ruleEs: Para revisar, cambia las palabras vagas por palabras exactas, agrega una palabra señal y agrega detalles que faltan.
learn.model: Draft: The bird is nice. Revised: The blue jay has bright feathers and a loud call.
learn.notice: The revised sentence has exact words like blue jay, bright feathers, and loud call.

items.prompt: Which sentence is the best revision of 'The plant is nice.'?

options.text: The plant is nice and good.
The plant is a plant.
The bean plant has bright green leaves.

items.why: A strong revision uses exact words you can picture. Bright green leaves tell the reader more than nice and good.
items.whyEs: Una buena revisión usa palabras exactas que puedes imaginar. Bright green leaves dice más que nice y good.

items.prompt: Choose the exact words to replace 'stuff' in the plant sentence.
items.model: The bean plant has green leaves and thin roots.
items.why: Words like stuff and things are vague. Green leaves is exact and shows the reader a picture.
items.whyEs: Palabras como stuff y things son vagas. Green leaves es exacto y le muestra una imagen al lector.

items.prompt: Which revision fixes the repeated words in 'The seed is small. The seed is round. The seed is brown.'?

options.text: The seed is small, round, and brown.
The seed small round brown.
The seed is small. The seed is round, and the seed is brown.

items.why: Joining the details in one sentence stops the repeated words. The other choices are not smooth or still repeat the seed.
items.whyEs: Unir los detalles en una oración evita repetir palabras. Las otras opciones no suenan bien o siguen repitiendo the seed.

items.prompt: Choose the signal word that links the two plant ideas.
items.model: The plant needs water. Also, it needs sunlight.
items.why: Also adds one more idea on the same topic. The other choices do not fit the meaning.
items.whyEs: Also agrega una idea más sobre el mismo tema. Las otras opciones no encajan con el significado.

items.prompt: Check the changes that make this draft stronger: 'The plant is nice. It has stuff. It grows.'

options.text: Change 'nice' to 'tall and green'.
Make every sentence shorter.
Change 'stuff' to 'leaves and roots'.
Add where it grows, like 'toward the sunny window'.
Use the word 'nice' two more times.

items.why: Exact words and added details make a draft stronger. Shorter sentences or repeating nice would not add any information.
items.whyEs: Las palabras exactas y los detalles agregados fortalecen un borrador. Oraciones más cortas o repetir nice no agregan información.

items.prompt: Put these revised sentences about a bean plant in order.
lines: First, it drinks water through its thin roots.
Next, it uses sunlight to make food in its leaves.
Finally, it makes a small flower.
items.why: The topic sentence comes first. Then first, next, and finally put the steps in the order they happen.
items.whyEs: La oración temática va primero. Luego first, next y finally ponen los pasos en el orden en que ocurren.

write.prompt: Revise the draft. Use exact words, add details, and add a signal word like first, next, or also.
write.promptEs: Revisa el borrador. Usa palabras exactas, agrega detalles y agrega una palabra señal como first, next o also.
write.text: The plant is nice. It has stuff. It grows.

label: I used a signal word like first, next, or also
Usé una palabra señal como first, next o also
I used exact words like leaves, roots, or sunlight
Usé palabras exactas como leaves, roots o sunlight

write.model: The bean plant grows tall. It has green leaves and thin roots. It also needs sunlight and water to grow.

familyTalk.en: Describe something at home without using the words 'nice' or 'good'. Use exact words instead.
familyTalk.es: Describan algo de la casa sin usar las palabras 'nice' o 'good'. Usen palabras exactas.

teacherTip.en: Circle the vague words in the draft together, then brainstorm exact replacements before students write.
teacherTip.es: Encierren juntos las palabras vagas del borrador y piensen reemplazos exactos antes de que escriban.

learn.rule: Strong writing names the exact place, person, or thing, and tells when. Signal words show the order.
learn.ruleEs: Una buena escritura nombra el lugar, la persona o la cosa exacta y dice cuándo. Las palabras señal muestran el orden.
learn.model: Draft: We went outside. Revised: On Monday, our class walked to the town park.
learn.notice: The revised sentence tells when, who, and exactly where.

items.prompt: Which sentence is the best revision of 'We went to the place.'?

options.text: We went to the place on a day.
Our class visited the post office.
We went to a spot.

items.why: A good revision names the exact place. Post office is exact, but place and spot are vague.
items.whyEs: Una buena revisión nombra el lugar exacto. Post office es exacto, pero place y spot son vagos.

items.prompt: Choose the exact words to replace 'a thing' in the sentence.
items.model: We saw a huge map on the wall.
items.why: A huge map is exact and helps the reader see the wall. A thing and stuff could be anything.
items.whyEs: A huge map es exacto y ayuda al lector a ver la pared. A thing y stuff pueden ser cualquier cosa.

items.prompt: Which revision fixes the repeated words in 'We saw a map. We saw a flag. We saw a statue.'?

options.text: We saw a map, a flag, and a statue.
We saw a map. Saw a flag. Saw a statue.
We saw a map and we saw a flag and we saw a statue.

items.why: Putting the list in one sentence stops the repeated words. The second choice has fragments and the third repeats we saw.
items.whyEs: Poner la lista en una oración evita repetir palabras. La segunda opción tiene fragmentos y la tercera repite we saw.

items.prompt: Choose the signal word that shows what happened second.
parts: First, we looked at old photos.
, we drew a picture of our favorite one.
items.model: First, we looked at old photos. Next, we drew a picture of our favorite one.
items.why: Next shows the order after first. Because and however would change the meaning of the sentence.
items.whyEs: Next muestra el orden después de first. Because y however cambiarían el significado de la oración.

items.prompt: Check the changes that make this draft stronger: 'We went to the place. We saw things. It was good.'

options.text: Name the place, like 'the town museum'.
Use the word 'good' in every sentence.
Add when it happened, like 'on Friday'.
Change 'things' to 'old tools'.
Make the draft shorter.

items.why: Exact places, times, and objects help a reader picture the trip. Repeating good or cutting words takes information away.
items.whyEs: Los lugares, los momentos y los objetos exactos ayudan al lector a imaginar la excursión. Repetir good o quitar palabras quita información.

items.prompt: Put these revised sentences about a post office visit in order.
lines: Our class visited the post office on Tuesday.
First, a worker showed us how letters are sorted.
Next, we watched a machine stamp the mail.
Finally, we wrote postcards to our families.
items.why: The opening sentence tells who, where, and when. Then first, next, and finally give the steps in order.
items.whyEs: La oración inicial dice quién, dónde y cuándo. Luego first, next y finally dan los pasos en orden.

write.prompt: Revise the draft. Name the place, tell when it happened, and use a signal word like then or next.
write.promptEs: Revisa el borrador. Nombra el lugar, di cuándo ocurrió y usa una palabra señal como then o next.
write.text: We went to the place. We saw things. It was good.

label: I used a signal word like then, next, or first
Usé una palabra señal como then, next o first
I named an exact place or thing
Nombré un lugar o una cosa exacta

write.model: Our class visited the town museum on Friday. We saw old tools and a huge map. Then we drew pictures of our favorite parts.

familyTalk.en: Tell about a place you visited. Say its exact name, when you went, and one thing you saw.
familyTalk.es: Cuenten sobre un lugar que visitaron. Digan su nombre exacto, cuándo fueron y una cosa que vieron.

teacherTip.en: Post a who, where, when chart so students can check that their revision names all three.
teacherTip.es: Pon un cartel de quién, dónde y cuándo para que los estudiantes revisen que su texto nombra los tres.

sets.title: Lila's Story Draft
sets.titleEs: El borrador del cuento de Lila

learn.rule: Make a story draft stronger by giving characters names, using exact feeling words, and telling what happens in order.
learn.ruleEs: Mejora el borrador de un cuento dando nombres a los personajes, usando palabras exactas para los sentimientos y contando en orden lo que pasa.
learn.model: Draft: The boy was happy. Revised: Omar was thrilled when his team scored the winning goal.
learn.notice: The revised sentence has a name, an exact feeling word, and a reason.

items.prompt: Which sentence is the best revision of 'The girl was sad.'?

options.text: The girl was very, very sad.
The girl was sad about stuff.
Lila felt lonely on her first day at the new school.

items.why: A strong revision gives a name, an exact feeling, and a reason. Adding very, very does not tell the reader anything new.
items.whyEs: Una buena revisión da un nombre, un sentimiento exacto y una razón. Agregar very, very no dice nada nuevo al lector.

items.prompt: Choose the exact action word for the sentence.
items.model: Lila tiptoed across the creaky floor.
items.why: Tiptoed shows exactly how Lila moved. Did a thing and went are vague.
items.whyEs: Tiptoed muestra exactamente cómo se movió Lila. Did a thing y went son vagos.

items.prompt: Choose the signal word that gives the reason.
parts: her kite was stuck in a tree.
items.model: Lila felt sad because her kite was stuck in a tree.
items.why: Because tells the reason for the feeling. Unless and until do not make sense here.
items.whyEs: Because dice la razón del sentimiento. Unless y until no tienen sentido aquí.

items.prompt: Which revision fixes the repeated words in 'Lila ran. Lila ran fast. Lila ran home.'?

options.text: Lila ran, and Lila ran fast, and Lila ran home.
Ran fast Lila home.
Lila ran fast all the way home.

items.why: One strong sentence says everything without repeating Lila ran. The other choices still repeat or are not a sentence.
items.whyEs: Una oración fuerte lo dice todo sin repetir Lila ran. Las otras opciones siguen repitiendo o no son oraciones.

items.prompt: Check the changes that make this draft stronger: 'The girl was sad. She did stuff. It was fine.'

options.text: Give the girl a name, like Lila.
Use the word 'stuff' again.
Say why she felt sad.
Tell what she did, like asking her brother for help.
Make every sentence only two words.

items.why: A name, a reason, and an exact action make the story clear. Repeating stuff or cutting sentences down takes details away.
items.whyEs: Un nombre, una razón y una acción exacta aclaran el cuento. Repetir stuff o acortar las oraciones quita detalles.

items.prompt: Put these revised story sentences about Lila's first day in order.
lines: Lila felt nervous about her first day at the new school.
First, she took a deep breath at the door.
Next, a boy named Omar smiled and waved.
Finally, Lila sat down and felt brave.
items.why: The first sentence sets up the feeling. Then first, next, and finally show the order of events.
items.whyEs: La primera oración presenta el sentimiento. Luego first, next y finally muestran el orden de los hechos.

write.prompt: Revise the draft. Give the girl a name, use an exact feeling word, and add a signal word like because or finally.
write.promptEs: Revisa el borrador. Dale un nombre a la niña, usa una palabra exacta para el sentimiento y agrega una palabra señal como because o finally.
write.text: The girl was sad. She did stuff. It was fine.

label: I used a signal word like because, then, or finally
Usé una palabra señal como because, then o finally
I used an exact feeling word or detail
Usé una palabra exacta de sentimiento o un detalle

write.model: Lila felt lonely because her kite got stuck in a tree. She asked her brother to help her. Finally, he climbed up and got it down.

familyTalk.en: Retell something that happened today using an exact feeling word, like proud, nervous, or excited.
familyTalk.es: Cuenten algo que pasó hoy usando una palabra exacta para el sentimiento, como proud, nervous o excited.

teacherTip.en: Keep a feelings word wall nearby so students can swap 'sad' and 'happy' for exact words.
teacherTip.es: Mantén cerca un muro de palabras de sentimientos para que los estudiantes cambien 'sad' y 'happy' por palabras exactas.
